newsitem.title: UK: EU seen cutting sugar output quotas by 2001.
newsitem.headline: EU seen cutting sugar output quotas by 2001.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is likely to cut its sugar production quotas and subsidised exports in the longer term due to constraints imposed on current policy, a leading sugar consultant said on Thursday.

"By the end of the current regime, it seems likely that change will begin to occur since exporting quota sugar will become subject to the GATT 21 percent quantitative and 36 percent budgetary constraints," Nicholas Child told a a conference in London hosted by Agra Europe.
Child is director of Brussels-based management consultants European Context Associates.

He said there would be a "very significant" reduction in subsidised exports in the long term and if this resulted in a higher world price, outside quota production might still be viable or even increase.
The EU's current sugar regime is valid until the end of June 2001.

"However, quota production will almost certainly have to contract, but the political trade-off will probably be the maintenance of a possibly single quota system with white sugar prices at a level which will satisfy Community producers, preferential exporters and permit some additional access."
